summary: Electronic Arts motorcycle combat racing series built around illegal street races, weapons, police, and later CD-era licensed soundtracks.

entries.title: Road Rash

emulation.notes: Use Genesis/Mega Drive emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: Road Rash debuted on Sega Genesis/Mega Drive and later received Amiga and scaled-down 8-bit/handheld ports. The Genesis version is the original, best-regarded route and was later preserved in EA Replay.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version in Genesis Plus GX, BlastEm, MiSTer, or original hardware; use EA Replay on PSP as a legal compilation route if owned.

all_releases.fidelity: Original 16-bit release and acclaimed debut route.
all_releases.reason: primary: original and best all-around route.

all_releases.fidelity: Home-computer port.
all_releases.reason: skip: slower/lower-impact alternate route and no sourced content advantage over Genesis.

all_releases.fidelity: Scaled-down 8-bit port.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity route and no sourced content advantage.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld Sega port.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity portable route.

all_releases.fidelity: Scaled-down handheld port, noted as incompatible with Game Boy Color/newer Game Boy hardware.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity handheld route.

all_releases.fidelity: EA Replay compilation release of the Genesis trilogy.
all_releases.reason: skip: compilation route, not a content upgrade over Genesis primary.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: No sourced platform-exclusive content requires a secondary route.

entries.remaster_caveats: SNES version was planned and canceled; EA Replay is a compilation route.

entries.title: Road Rash II

emulation.notes: Use Genesis/Mega Drive emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: Road Rash II is a Genesis/Mega Drive sequel adding simultaneous split-screen, Mano a Mano, nitro bikes, chains, and U.S. locations. Later GBC/PSP/Genesis Mini routes are ports or compilation hardware.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version in Genesis Plus GX, BlastEm, MiSTer, original hardware, or the Genesis Mini/EA Replay if owned.

all_releases.fidelity: Original 16-bit release with split-screen and Mano a Mano modes.
all_releases.reason: primary: original and complete route.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld conversion released as Road Rash.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity handheld conversion and no sourced content advantage.

all_releases.fidelity: EA Replay compilation release.
all_releases.reason: skip: compilation route, not a content upgrade over Genesis primary.

all_releases.fidelity: Mini-console reissue of the Genesis game.
all_releases.reason: skip: convenient reissue hardware, not a content upgrade.

entries.remaster_caveats: Master System and Game Gear versions were announced but not released.

entries.title: Road Rash

emulation.emulator: Native Windows / VM / 3DO emulator / DuckStation / Mednafen Saturn
emulation.notes: Use Windows for primary; emulate 3DO for original presentation comparison.

primary.why: The CD-era Road Rash released first for 3DO, then Sega CD, PlayStation, Saturn, and Windows. Windows keeps the CD-era FMV/licensed soundtrack framework and adds online multiplayer for up to eight players over modem or LAN, making it the most complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Windows 95 version on a compatibility setup or VM; use 3DO emulation for the original CD-console presentation.

all_releases.fidelity: Original CD-era release with digitized actors, FMV, and licensed soundtrack.
all_releases.reason: skip: best original CD-console reference, but Windows adds sourced online multiplayer.

all_releases.fidelity: Sega CD version developed as a bridge between the 3DO game and Road Rash 3.
all_releases.reason: skip: downgraded/alternate CD route, no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: PlayStation port of the CD-era game.
all_releases.reason: skip: later port, no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Saturn port of the CD-era game.
all_releases.reason: skip: later port, no sourced content advantage over Windows.

all_releases.fidelity: Windows 95 version with online multiplayer for up to eight players over modem or LAN.
all_releases.reason: primary: most complete CD-era route.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: 3DO is the original acclaimed CD-console route, while Windows adds the sourced multiplayer feature and higher PC ceiling.

entries.remaster_caveats: This is the CD-era Road Rash, distinct from the 1991 Genesis original and 2009 Java title.

entries.title: Road Rash 3

emulation.notes: Use Genesis/Mega Drive emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: Road Rash 3 is a Genesis/Mega Drive-only worldwide sequel and the final Road Rash released for Genesis, adding global locations, bike upgrades, and persistent/multiple weapons.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Genesis/Mega Drive version in Genesis Plus GX, BlastEm, MiSTer, original hardware, or EA Replay if owned.

all_releases.fidelity: Only original release platform.
all_releases.reason: primary: only original route and complete game.

all_releases.fidelity: EA Replay compilation release of the Genesis trilogy.
all_releases.reason: skip: compilation route, not a content upgrade over Genesis primary.

entries.remaster_caveats: EA Replay is a compilation route.

entries.title: Road Rash 3D

emulation.notes: Use high internal resolution for modern play.

primary.why: Road Rash 3D is a PlayStation-exclusive 3D entry with interconnected road-grid courses and licensed music, but less emphasis on combat than earlier games.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version in DuckStation at high internal resolution.

all_releases.fidelity: Only released platform; 3D engine with licensed soundtrack.
all_releases.reason: primary: only release route and complete game.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: Single-platform release; planned PC version was not released.

entries.remaster_caveats: Planned PC version with LAN multiplayer and force-feedback support was canceled.

entries.title: Road Rash 64

emulation.notes: Enable Expansion Pak features where supported.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: N64 high-resolution mode with emulator scaling

primary.version: Nintendo 64 release with Expansion Pak options
primary.why: Road Rash 64 is a Nintendo 64-only entry with a greater combat focus, interconnected routes, Cop Mode, several multiplayer modes, and Expansion Pak graphics options.
primary.how_to_play: Play in a Nintendo 64 emulator with Expansion Pak enabled, or on original hardware.

all_releases.fidelity: Only released platform; Expansion Pak adds alternate graphics, widescreen, letterbox, and high-resolution settings.
all_releases.reason: primary: only release route and highest display option.

entries.remaster_caveats: Not developed or published by EA; THQ published it under license.

entries.title: Road Rash: Jailbreak

emulation.notes: Use PlayStation emulation for the primary route.

primary.why: Road Rash: Jailbreak released on PlayStation, then received a Game Boy Advance handheld port. The PlayStation version is the higher-fidelity main route and includes the sidecar-focused cooperative play direction.
primary.how_to_play: Play the PlayStation version in DuckStation; use GBA only for portable comparison.

all_releases.fidelity: Original console release.
all_releases.reason: primary: higher-fidelity main route.

all_releases.fidelity: Handheld port with the same title.
all_releases.reason: skip: lower-fidelity handheld route and no sourced content advantage over PlayStation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Final traditional console entry in the series; GBA port is a handheld route.

entries.title: Road Rash

emulation.notes: Use Java mobile preservation tools or original hardware.

primary.why: Road Rash was released for J2ME in 2009 and sold through EA Mobile. It has only one sourced platform route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on compatible Java mobile hardware or a preserved J2ME emulator setup where available.

all_releases.fidelity: EA Mobile Java release.
all_releases.reason: primary: only sourced release route.

entries.remaster_caveats: Distinct mobile entry, not the 1991 or 1994 Road Rash game.
